If you following them doctrines, them philosophies, them lies, that man going to be the prophet to you, a prophet to lead you right to hell. A lot of these wicked pastors just chasing money and don't care about the people's souls, about healing the people and bringing them back to Christ.
precepts.point: We got the power to bring our people back to God, and we refuse to do it because we selfish, greedy, covetous, and we love preeminence in this place. This place taught us how to go against our God, but we teaching our people how to come back to him in righteousness. It's going to be a great fight, but this fight going to be won.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” We are an afflicted people, and we haven’t realized it yet. We are being put through the wringer because we constantly break his law of commandments, because we departed from God, because we don’t know who we are, and because God has been calling us and we refuse to turn around and come back to him. And we are drunken, but not with wine. Drunken with what? Micah shows it.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” We are drunk with philosophy and doctrines, the lies we learned here in America. If you follow those doctrines, those laws, those philosophies, those lies, that man is going to be the prophet to you: a prophet to lead you right to hell.

A lot of these wicked and evil pastors are just chasing money, money, money, and don’t give a damn about the people’s souls or their spirits. They don’t care about healing the people, fixing the people and bringing them back to Christ. The people are crying, looking for Christ, and these men mislead them while chasing the dollar bill. Let those men be your prophet if you are going to believe that garbage.

That is why we have gangs in the street, prostitutes in the street, our sons fainted and lying “at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”: the dead Israelites in the churches are not teaching our people how to keep the Lord’s commandments or how to come back to Christ. But the Lord who “pleadeth the cause of his people” says he has taken the cup of trembling out of our hand, and “I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee.”

precepts.text: The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart. Some of our young men are mentally deranged under the curses, and the music glorifies it.
precepts.point: And thou hast laid thy body as the ground: our people will weep publicly for men who never said or did anything for them, but will not cry for each other. That is Isaiah 51:23 in action.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. That is why our young men hang on the corners: uncontrollable, like wild bulls in a net. It's a trap; this system is a trap. “they are full of the fury of the Lord”. What is the fury of the Lord? Deuteronomy 28:15-68, the curses God put upon us, and they are on our young men.

Even this one: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Some of our young men are mentally deranged. The ones doing that new type of singing, drill: they are murderers, they are killers, and they don't care.

It is seen in the neighborhood. A house in Queens, a playground across the street with about twenty adorable little kids running around. Time went by, those little kids grew up, and they were having shootouts, bullets flying through the house, the kids and the wife thrown on the floor. That is what they turned into.

So the sons fainted at the head of all the streets are the sons of Israel under the curse of madness. They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God, and that is why they cannot be controlled.

precepts.text: If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people. Wine there symbolizes lies: that is what our people are drunk with.
precepts.point: And thou hast laid thy body as the ground: our people will weep publicly for men who never said or did anything for them, but will not cry for each other. That is Isaiah 51:23 in action.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine”. We are an afflicted people: look at the news, and we are afflicted from sun up to sun down, over and over. You can turn a blind eye to it, but it's there. And we are a drunk people. What does it mean we're drunk? We're drunk with lies, drunk with religions, drunk with falsehood.

Micah shows that wine represents falsehood: “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” Wine and strong drink symbolize lies. The man walking in falsehood prophesies lies, and he becomes the prophet of this people.

So what are we drunk with? Lies. Some of us believe in these false Christian religions, Islam, politics; we're drunk in some philosophy out here. But the Lord “pleadeth the cause of his people”, and he says “I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling”. That is why we are waking up now. “even the dregs of the cup of my fury”: the dregs is the bottom, the last few drops left in the cup. “thou shalt no more drink it again” after this captivity is over. He will put it into the hand of them that afflict us, Esau and the nations.

precepts.text: Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net. When Peter explained the fourfooted beasts and wild beasts, he would have to refer to these scriptures: remember, it is written that we lived as beasts, that we were as a wild bull.
precepts.point: Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had. The vessel knit at the four corners is Israel, and the beasts within it are men. This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it, they think it is everybody. No: God said Israel was the vessel.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
The vessel also held “wild beasts.” Isaiah names them: “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God.”

The sons of Israel, fainted and lying at the head of every street, are compared to a wild bull caught in a net, full of the fury of the Lord. The wild beast is a man of Israel under God's rebuke.

When Peter explained the fourfooted beasts and wild beasts, he would have to refer to scriptures like these. Remember, it is written in 2 Esdras that we lived as beasts. Remember, it is written in Psalms that we were as beasts. Remember, Isaiah the prophet said we would be as a wild bull. The vision was about men, and the scriptures prove it.

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors: when you learn from their examples, it gives us a guide for today. That is called legacy.
precepts.point: They ignorantly call themselves young ones in the streets, and this generation culture is not your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings? When we bethink, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Isaiah 51:20 says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. What other people on the planet are at the head of every corner on the streets? That's us: in Miami, in the Bronx, in all the hoods and all the ghettos throughout the whole earth. We fainted, we are hid in prison houses, and we are on every corner. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

precepts.text: The Most High called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him.
precepts.point: Confessing Christ before men means something. When Christ asked, Whom say ye that I am, Peter confessed, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; whoever confesses Him before men, He confesses before His Father, and He came to set a man at variance against his own household for the truth's sake.

note.label: Genesis 12: The Calling of Abram

precepts.why:
The Most High told Abram to get out of his country, from his kindred and from his father's house. Isaiah says how he was called: “Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.”

He called Abraham alone, and blessed him, and increased him. Some hold back from repenting because of what family or friends may say. Do not let your kindred hold you back from being blessed and increased; when the Most High calls you out, you have to go.

precepts.text: I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die? The chosen people of the living God have no business fearing a man who will be made as grass.
precepts.point: The Most High put laws in the book about going to battle, and this fear showed that Saul and the people lacked faith; the same God that destroyed Pharaoh and the Egyptians who pursued Israel was with them, and a trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
“I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass”. The chosen people of the living God have no business fearing a man who will be made as grass.

A trial of faith was set before them in the form of one big intimidating man with a big mouth, and they were dismayed.

precepts.text: He will put the cup in the hand of them that afflicted thee, who said bow down that we may go over, and thou hast laid thy body as the ground.
precepts.point: The face is hidden because of iniquity. Sins separate us from the Most High so that He will not hear.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“For our soul is bowed down to the dust: our belly cleaveth unto the earth.” Isaiah shows who made us bow: “But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.”

They said to our soul, bow down that we may go over, and we laid our body as the ground and as the street for them to walk on. We were once at a higher state and were brought low. But the Most High will put the cup into the hand of them that afflicted us; that is him arising for our help and redeeming us for his mercies' sake.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: “Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return, and come with singing unto Zion;” So we're going to return to the land with singing unto Zion. “and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away.” That is the comfort for all that mourn: the mourning flees away when we return.
